subject: computer-science
title: Programming Paradigms: OO vs Functional
welcome_lead: Two giants of modern programming compared.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: object-oriented vs functional, pure functions and state.
final_note: Each paradigm shines on different kinds of problem.

concepts.def: A paradigm based on objects bundling state and behaviour.
A paradigm built from pure functions and immutable data.
A function with no side effects whose output depends only on inputs.
The property of values that cannot be changed after creation.
A function that takes or returns another function.
Data that persists and can change during program execution.

walkthroughs.body_html: OO bundles state and behaviour into objects. The four pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction. Java, C# and C++ are mainstream OO languages.

Functional programming favours pure functions — same input, same output, no side effects. Data is immutable. Haskell, Lisp and Erlang are functional; modern JS and Python borrow many functional features.

OO suits systems modelled as entities with behaviour (GUIs, simulations). Functional suits transformations of data (analytics, concurrency) because pure functions are easy to reason about and run in parallel.
